title: The return given to the State and the return e-filed with the IRS
question: Is the copy of the federal return a charity files with the Attorney General the same as the one the IRS holds?
finding: 82 copies of returns in the registry files could be placed beside an e-filed return for the same year. 79 agree on revenue and expenses (to within $25,000). 3 are a first version that the organization later amended with the IRS, and 0 match no version the IRS holds. 6 summary pages could not be read reliably (revenue less expenses did not equal the printed difference) and are not counted.
how: Total revenue (line 12) and total expenses (line 18) are read from the summary page of each return in the registry files and matched to the e-filed returns of the same employer number: first on both figures, then on either. Where both figures match an earlier e-filed version but not the latest, the row shows the State copy beside the latest IRS version.
limits: An amended federal return is ordinary and the State copy was true to the first filing when sent; whether the amended version was also sent to the State can be seen only on the registry's list. Figures read from scanned pages can be misread. Returns for years before 2020 cannot be compared because the IRS files on disk start there. See also the amended-returns screen in "Do the two sets of books agree?".
